title: Object-Oriented Programming Principles
learningObjectives: Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Object-oriented programming organizes code around objects that combine state and behavior. Encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance and polymorphism are common OOP concepts.
understand.whyItMatters: OOP can model domain entities and separate responsibilities into cooperating types.
understand.explain: Understand each concept separately and choose object-based design only when it clarifies behavior.

examples.title: Encapsulate state and action
examples.code: class Lamp{public:void turnOn(){on=true;}bool isOn()const{return on;}private:bool on=false;};\nLamp l;l.turnOn();
examples.explanation: Object combines state and behavior behind an interface.

examples.title: Abstraction
examples.explanation: Client calls a simple operation without needing its internal steps.

examples.title: Separate responsibilities
examples.explanation: Cart owns one cohesive responsibility: items.

examples.title: Inheritance relation concept
examples.code: class Animal{public:void eat(){}};class Dog:public Animal{};\nDog d;d.eat();
examples.explanation: Derived Dog inherits the public Animal operation.

examples.title: Polymorphic interface
examples.explanation: Abstract interface requires derived shapes to provide area.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Object-Oriented Programming Principles examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating object-oriented programming principles in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.
